ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left of the figure is equilateral triangle VWX, with WX as the base and vertex V above; on the right is equilateral triangle XYZ, and side XY connects from X upward to the right to Y. The segment WY is also drawn in the figure, and WY lies inside angle VWX starting from W. The labeled 80° is the angle at point X formed by XV and XY, namely ∠VXY. Reasoning: Because VWX and XYZ are congruent equilateral triangles, each interior angle is 60°, and corresponding side lengths are equal, in particular WX = XY. In the left equilateral triangle, ∠VXW = 60°. From the order of the rays in the figure, ∠WXY is composed of ∠WXV and ∠VXY, so ∠WXY = 60° + 80° = 140°. In triangle WXY, WX = XY, so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, so ∠YWX = ∠WYX = (180° - 140°)/2 = 20°. Also because ∠VWX = 60°, and WY lies inside ∠VWX, ∠VWY = ∠VWX - ∠YWX = 60° - 20° = 40°.

raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, $VWX$ and $XYZ$ are congruent equilateral triangles and $\angle VXY = 80^{\circ}$. What is the size of $\angle VWY$?

method.method_draft: Synthetic angle chase using the isosceles triangle WXY. From the image, note that W, X are joined as the base of triangle VWX, X is joined to Y as a side of triangle XYZ, and segment WY is drawn inside angle VWX. From the text, use that VWX and XYZ are congruent equilateral triangles, so each angle in triangle VWX is 60 degrees and the common side length gives WX = XY. Since angle VXW is 60 degrees and the marked angle VXY is 80 degrees, the angle WXY is 60 + 80 = 140 degrees as shown by the ordering of rays XW, XV, XY in the diagram. Then triangle WXY is isosceles with WX = XY, so its base angles are (180 - 140)/2 = 20 degrees. Thus angle YWV = angle VWX - angle YWX = 60 - 20 = 40 degrees.

Because VWX is equilateral, V lies in direction 60 degrees from W and ray XV points at direction 120 degrees from the positive x-axis. From the text, angle VXY = 80 degrees, and the image shows ray XY on the upper-right side of X, so ray XY has direction 120 degrees - 80 degrees = 40 degrees from the positive x-axis. Since XYZ is congruent equilateral to VWX, XY has length 1, so Y = (1 + cos 40 degrees, sin 40 degrees). The direction of WY from W has slope sin 40/(1 + cos 40) = tan 20, so ray WY makes a 20-degree angle with WX. Ray WV makes a 60-degree angle with WX, hence angle VWY = 60 - 20 = 40 degrees.
